doc.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: What gigs may not return and rediscovering guitarists on YouTube
summary: He expects small venues to disappear and says the time at home lets him revisit guitarists such as Rene Thomas and Oscar Aleman on YouTube.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You are anticipating a question I had and that is let’s suppose the situation very suddenly got better and things returned, are there activities, types of gigs and so forth, that you might choose to not do again, that you were doing before?

I would question getting on an airplane for gigs that aren’t really on a certain level. And I’ve kind of graduated from doing the smaller gigs over the years, the smaller gigs, to more of the performing arts centers and you know, higher levels of jazz clubs and stuff like that. So I think I’ve been more selective about where I’d be playing. But the reality is that some of the smaller gigs are just going to go away. I mean some of these businesses are not going to be able to maintain their premises or whatever their business model is, is severely disrupted by all the shutdowns. I mean there are clubs around L.A. that I don’t know are going to reopen. And on the acoustic guitar circuit there are a lot of more intimate venues that can’t necessarily survive. So I think it’s going to be a different era when we do come out of this. But I think that my focus is, having the time and not having to deal with travel has given me more of an opportunity to really focus on music and being able to, whether it’s following up on guitar players that I used to listen to and haven’t listened to in some years and I’ll go on YouTube and then go down the YouTube rabbit hole. Like for example I’d long forgotten René Thomas who is a Belgian guitar player that worked with Stan Getz, who I would enjoy listening to thirty, forty years ago, and I you know, I had a portion of my record collection was stolen in the mid 70s and as a result there are certain records that I’d just forgotten about. And being able to find stuff on YouTube has been — because I’m a perpetual student of music and of guitar. And to be able to, you know, find video let’s say of Oscar Aleman, who you know, is not necessarily as well known as Django Reinhardt, but is a great guitar player, and Josephine Baker’s musical director.
I did not know that, and I have to admit I had not heard this name.
